reason: The text explicitly portrays elite members unfavorably. The passage identifies 250 'nesi'ei eda' (chiefs/leaders of the congregation) and 'anshei shem' (men of renown) who join Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron. These elite figures are described as 'anashim reshayim' (wicked men), directly challenge divinely appointed leadership out of envy and ambition, and face severe divine punishment—the earth swallows some alive into Sheol while fire consumes the 250 who offered incense. The narrative structure uses their rebellion, punishment, and destruction as a cautionary tale against elite presumption and resistance to God's chosen leaders.
